transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Angela Ruiz (CTO, NorthRidge), Samir Khan (Lead ML Eng), Tina Lopez (IT)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of Redwood's Model Catalog UI in Console, discussion of open model selection and recommended benchmarks, compatibility matrix for their on-prem cluster (VPC / dedicated vs hosted), and follow-up pilot actions. Security and compliance questions on SOC2, SSO, KMS covered at a high level.

Topics:
- Model catalog: filters, tags, benchmarks
- API vs Console usage for selection and evaluation
- Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization, batching, KV cache)
- Compatibility matrix for NorthRidge infra (CUDA, tensor cores, quantized weights)
- Security: SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS, audit logs
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we got about 45 minutes, i'll do a quick run through the model catalog and then marcus will dig into the compatibility and perf stuff - sound good?
[00:18] Angela Ruiz: yep that works for us, thanks. we, um, we're especially interested in how to pick open models that balance cost and accuracy for summarization and clinical note generation.
[00:32] Marcus Patel: perfect, we'll show the catalog filters, benchmark badges, and then the compatibility matrix that maps to your on-prem gpus, also talk about dedicated vs hosted.
[00:45] Samir Khan: quick note, we have A100 and some T4s in our colo, and our app is latency sensitive for patient triage flows, so 200-300ms p95 is ideal.
[00:58] Tina Lopez: and we need to keep PHI in our VPC, so private deployment options are a must, plus KMS integration.
[01:12] Laura Chen: totally got it. okay jumping into the Console - the model catalog home page shows curated models, open-source variants, and redwood-verified performance profiles. you can filter by task (summarization, chat, embedding), by cost tier, and by compute compatibility.
[01:35] Marcus Patel: one thing to call out, the benchmark badges are empirical — e.g., latency on 8k context for a given GPU, mem footprint, and also rt-quality scores from our eval harness. sometimes the badge names get munged in transcription, but they'll be on the sheet we send.
[01:52] Angela Ruiz: can you show an example for, say, the Llama-2 variants? we're concerned about quantized models and hallucination.
[02:05] Marcus Patel: yeah so here we filter for Llama-2 and Med-small models; you'll notice compatibility flags: fp16, int8, awq, and whether kv cache is supported for long context. for hallucination mitigation we recommend the model+prompt eval sets — you can run them via the Console or the API.
[02:28] Laura Chen: and in the Console you can click 'Compare' and select up to four models to see side-by-side benchmark metrics — tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, and a cost-per-1000-token estimate.
[02:43] Samir Khan: that cost estimate, is that for hosted only or does it factor in dedicated GPU e2e cost?
[02:52] Laura Chen: good question. the estimate has two modes: hosted (our public API pricing) and dedicated (a normalized per-token cost based on reserved capacity settings). we also provide a 'real cost' calculator if you want to include infra specifics.
[03:08] Tina Lopez: about private deployment — how does the compatibility matrix work for air-gapped or on-prem installs?
[03:17] Marcus Patel: the matrix includes binary compatibility rows — OS, CUDA, cuDNN, driver versions, and also recommended quantization pathways. if you run, say, AWQ-8bit we mark which kernels we ship for that GPU. for air-gapped we have an on-prem bundle and installer guide (link shared in chat).
[03:35] Angela Ruiz: can we get that matrix mapped to our A100s and T4s?
[03:40] Marcus Patel: yes we'll export a CSV — we'll run a matching pass with your inventory. i'll need the exact driver versions and kernel info.
[03:49] Samir Khan: we'll share that after the call.
[03:52] Laura Chen: perfect. moving on to benchmarks: if you want accurate numbers we recommend two steps — a small smoke test via hosted API to validate quality, then a dedicated perf run in your infra using our perf harness.
[04:10] Marcus Patel: i'll run a benchmark with your sample dataset — we can replicate request patterns and measure p95. expect differences when using quantized models; sometimes int8 reduces quality slightly but cuts latency and cost.
[04:25] Angela Ruiz: what's your approach to KV cache for long context? we've got some notes that need 8k windows for summarization.
[04:32] Marcus Patel: we support streaming KV cache and prefix caching; the model catalog flags which models have efficient kv cache implementations. for workloads with repeated prefixes, prefix caching can shave off a lot of tokens and reduce cost.
[04:47] Laura Chen: also check Optimize — it gives recommendations like batch size tuning, quantization profiles, and caching policy suggestions based on observed traffic. it's interactive in the Console, and you can request 'apply' to an environment.
[05:02] Samir Khan: does Optimize handle mixed model routing? e.g., route quick triage to a smaller model and fall back to a larger one for complex cases?
[05:12] Marcus Patel: yes, smart routing policies can do that — latency-first vs cost-first policies, with automatic fallback. you can define thresholds in the Console.
[05:20] Tina Lopez: security: can you confirm SSO and audit logging for Private deployments?
[05:26] Laura Chen: yes, SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC, and detailed audit logs retained per your plan. KMS integration for key management is supported, including cloud KMS and HSM options for on-prem.
[05:40] Angela Ruiz: SOC2 evidence — do you share the reports?
[05:44] Laura Chen: we can share SOC2 Type II and the security pack under NDA. i'll attach the pack to the doc we send.
[05:53] Samir Khan: any limitations on model fine-tuning or using private data to further specialize models?
[05:59] Marcus Patel: for hosted we offer fine-tuning with strict data controls; for Private you can run fine-tune or adapter flows in your infra. we recommend adapter-style or LoRA variants if you want lighter weight.
[06:12] Angela Ruiz: ok, demo the API flow for selecting a model and running a benchmark.
[06:18] Laura Chen: sure — in the API quickstart we show sample requests; you can pick model id from the catalog, then call /v1/generate with streaming or non-streaming. i'm pasting a link to the quickstart in the chat.
[06:33] Marcus Patel: showing the perf harness repo — it's open-source, we use it for benchmark runs. note, results vary a bit depending on driver versions, and transcription sometimes shows model names wrong, like 'Llama two' instead of Llama-2, just FYI.
[06:48] Samir Khan: about quantization — you mentioned AWQ and GPTQ, which do you recommend for A100?
[06:55] Marcus Patel: for A100 we typically recommend fp16 for best accuracy/latency, and AWQ int8 if you need cost reductions; GPTQ can be good but depends on the model architecture. the compatibility matrix will show which quantization paths we validated.
[07:10] Angela Ruiz: can the Console export a comparison CSV for the models we select?
[07:16] Laura Chen: yep, export as CSV or JSON; we'll attach that to the follow-up.
[07:22] Tina Lopez: on the networking side, do you support private endpoints for API calls into our VPC?
[07:27] Marcus Patel: yes, private endpoints and VPC peering for dedicated/private deployments. for hosted API we can do IP allowlist and customer-managed VPC egress.
[07:40] Samir Khan: is there any SLA around latency?
[07:44] Laura Chen: dedicated offers SLA-backed latency targets depending on reserved capacity; hosted has best-effort but we publish performance profiles. We'll include the SLA appendix in the follow-up.
[07:56] Angela Ruiz: what's the expected timeline for a pilot? we need a pilot within 2-3 weeks ideally.
[08:03] Laura Chen: that's doable — typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: baseline smoke test, perf run, and a small production trial. we'll try to start the kickoff week of 2026-03-17.
[08:16] Marcus Patel: note, to get accurate p95 numbers i need your sample dataset and the node/gpu driver details.
[08:23] Samir Khan: we'll send those.
[08:27] Laura Chen: any other vendor concerns?
[08:30] Angela Ruiz: we are also evaluating Anthropic for safety features, and OpenAI for ease of use, reasoning about cost.
[08:38] Marcus Patel: understood. our differentiation is the unified serving runtime plus the Optimize tooling for cost/perf tuning, and the ability to run the same config in private or dedicated modes.
[08:50] Tina Lopez: last question, is there an install window for on-prem? downtime?
[08:55] Marcus Patel: the on-prem agent installs with minimal disruption; for air-gapped we schedule an install window and provide scripts — depends on cluster size.
[09:05] Laura Chen: okay wrapping up — recap and next steps. we'll send the model-compat matrix, pricing sheet, SOC2 and security pack, and a recorded version of this demo. Marcus will run the perf test with your dataset and return numbers, and we'll aim to schedule the pilot kickoff week of the 17th.
[09:25] Angela Ruiz: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:29] Samir Khan: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:31] Tina Lopez: thanks, bye.

References shared in chat: link: https://redwood.ai/docs/model-catalog, perf harness repo: https://github.com/redwood/perf-harness (note: placeholder links), security pack (will be sent under NDA).

End of transcript.
